meta.description: Real JEE organic chemistry chosen to exercise every feature. Unverified: no record is marked verified.

concept.name: E2
concept.summary: Bimolecular elimination: base removes a β-hydrogen as the leaving group departs.

concept.name: Markovnikov's rule
concept.summary: In the addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens.

concept.name: Saytzeff's rule
concept.summary: The more substituted alkene is the major elimination product.

concept.name: SN2
concept.summary: Bimolecular nucleophilic substitution: one concerted step with backside attack.

species.notes: Unstable above about 5 °C in solution; used as prepared.
Configuration unspecified: a mixture or unstated geometry.

reasons: Deliberately has a very long IUPAC name and no structure; the name is entered from memory and needs checking.
Structure is deliberately unparsable: exercises CHEM-001 when the chemistry worker exists (phase 4).

species.notes: Long unbranched chain: exercises structure depiction of long chains.

properties.value: Weakly acidic; more acidic than alcohols

class.description: Compounds with a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon.
Hydrocarbons with a carbon–carbon double bond.
Hydrocarbons with a carbon–carbon triple bond.

profiles.label: Warm, aldehyde distilled off
profiles.behaviour: Limited oxidant with the product removed as it forms.

profiles.label: Aqueous KOH
profiles.behaviour: Hydroxide acts mainly as a nucleophile.

profiles.label: Alcoholic KOH
profiles.behaviour: The alkoxide/hydroxide acts mainly as a base.

reagent.description: One reagent, two ways of using it: aqueous KOH substitutes, alcoholic KOH eliminates.
A poisoned palladium catalyst: hydrogenation stops at the alkene.
Pyridinium chlorochromate: a mild, anhydrous oxidant.

profiles.label: Baeyer's reagent
profiles.behaviour: Hydroxylates C=C; the purple colour fades and brown MnO₂ forms.

profiles.label: Hot, concentrated
profiles.behaviour: Cleaves C=C to carbonyl compounds and acids.

reagent.description: Used concentrated as a dehydrating agent and acid catalyst.

named_reaction.name: Aldol reaction
named_reaction.summary: An enolisable carbonyl compound adds to another carbonyl compound to give a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound.

named_reaction.name: Beckmann rearrangement
named_reaction.summary: An oxime rearranges to an amide (a lactam from a cyclic oxime) in acid.

named_reaction.name: Cannizzaro reaction
named_reaction.summary: Aldehydes with no α-hydrogen disproportionate in concentrated alkali to an alcohol and a carboxylate.

named_reaction.name: Diazotisation
named_reaction.summary: Primary aromatic amine to diazonium salt with nitrous acid at 0–5 °C.

named_reaction.name: Fischer esterification
named_reaction.summary: Acid-catalysed equilibrium between a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol and an ester plus water.

named_reaction.name: Grignard reaction
named_reaction.summary: An organomagnesium halide adds to a carbonyl group; work-up gives an alcohol.

named_reaction.name: Haloform reaction
named_reaction.summary: Methyl ketones and compounds oxidised to them give a haloform with a halogen and alkali.

named_reaction.name: Lindlar reduction
named_reaction.summary: Partial hydrogenation of an alkyne to a cis-alkene.

named_reaction.name: Sandmeyer reaction
named_reaction.summary: Diazonium group replaced by Cl, Br or CN using the copper(I) salt.

mechanism.name: Aldol addition of ethanal
mechanism.summary: A carbonyl compound with α-hydrogens adds, through its enol or enolate, to a second carbonyl group.

variants.label: Base-catalysed
variants.applicability: Dilute alkali, low temperature: the aldol is isolated.

steps.title: Hydroxide removes an α-hydrogen to give the enolate
Enolate carbon attacks a second ethanal

variants.label: Acid-catalysed
variants.applicability: Acid catalyst: enol is the nucleophile; condensation to but-2-enal is easy on heating.

steps.title: Enol forms by loss of an α-hydrogen
Loss of H⁺ gives the aldol

reasons: Mechanism steps and atom maps were entered by hand; verify before marking verified.

mechanism.name: E2 elimination of a haloalkane
mechanism.summary: One concerted step: base removes a β-hydrogen as the halide leaves.

variants.label: Saytzeff elimination (small base)
variants.applicability: Small base such as ethoxide or hydroxide in alcohol: the more substituted alkene is major.

steps.title: β-Hydrogen removed from the more substituted carbon
steps.description: Base removes the β-hydrogen while the C=C forms and the halide leaves, all in one step, anti-periplanar.

variants.label: Hofmann-type elimination (bulky base)
variants.applicability: Bulky base or poor leaving group: the less substituted alkene can predominate.

steps.title: β-Hydrogen removed from the less hindered carbon
steps.description: Base removes the β-hydrogen while the C=C forms and the halide leaves, all in one step, anti-periplanar.

reasons: Mechanism steps and atom maps were entered by hand; verify before marking verified.

mechanism.name: SN2 substitution of a haloalkane
mechanism.summary: One concerted step: the nucleophile enters from the side opposite the leaving group.

variants.label: Concerted backside attack
variants.applicability: Primary and secondary haloalkanes with a good nucleophile in a polar protic or aprotic solvent.

steps.title: Hydroxide attacks the carbon opposite the leaving group

reasons: Mechanism steps and atom maps were entered by hand; verify before marking verified.

reaction.name: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (PCC)
reaction.studyNotes: PCC in anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ stops at the aldehyde; there is no water to form the hydrate that would be oxidised further.

reaction.name: Diazotisation of aniline
reaction.limitations: Above about 5 °C the diazonium salt decomposes; use it at once.

reaction.name: Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde
reaction.limitations: Only aldehydes with no α-hydrogen; acidification of the sodium salt gives the carboxylic acid.

participants.note: Used up: it binds to the ketone product, so it is not a catalyst here.

reaction.name: Nitration of benzene (draft)
reaction.notes: Draft with no product yet: exercises RXN-002 at draft severity.

reaction.name: Benzenediazonium chloride → phenol
reaction.studyNotes: Taught in both the amines and the phenols chapters.

reaction.name: But-2-yne + H₂ (Lindlar)

stereochemistry.note: Both hydrogens add to the same face of the triple bond.

reaction.limitations: The poisoned catalyst stops at the alkene; ordinary Pd/C goes on to the alkane.

reasons: Deliberately unanchored (no class on its species) and mapped outside JEE Main scope; scope is unverified.

reversibility.note: The aldol can revert (retro-aldol); heating leads on to but-2-enal.

conditionVariants.label: 413 K, excess ethanol
conditionVariants.note: Two ethanol molecules lose one water.

reversibility.note: Ethene can be hydrated back to ethanol under other conditions.

reaction.name: Ethanol → ethanal (K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺, distillation)

stages.originalText: Distil the ethanal off as it forms

reaction.limitations: The aldehyde is oxidised further unless it is distilled out of the mixture at once.

products.note: Brown precipitate; the purple colour fades.

reaction.name: Acid-catalysed hydration of ethene

reversibility.note: The reverse is acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol.

reaction.limitations: Industrial conditions; in the laboratory the alkene is absorbed in cold conc. H₂SO₄ and the mixture is then diluted and warmed.

reversibility.note: Excess water pushes the equilibrium towards the acid and alcohol.

reaction.name: Fischer esterification: ethanoic acid + ethanol

reversibility.note: Driven to the ester by excess alcohol or by removing water.

reaction.studyNotes: The reverse reaction is acid-catalysed ester hydrolysis.

reaction.name: Iodoform test: ethanol

products.note: Yellow precipitate with an antiseptic smell.

reaction.limitations: Ethanol is the only primary alcohol that responds: it is first oxidised to ethanal, a methyl carbonyl compound.

outcomes.label: Markovnikov product
outcomes.rationale: H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens; the more stable secondary carbocation forms.

reaction.name: Propene + HBr (peroxide)

outcomes.label: Anti-Markovnikov product
outcomes.rationale: A bromine radical adds first, giving the more stable secondary radical.

reaction.limitations: Only HBr shows the peroxide effect; HCl and HI do not.

outcomes.label: Saytzeff product
outcomes.rationale: The more substituted alkene is more stable.

stereochemistry.note: Backside attack inverts the stereocentre: R gives S.

caveat.title: AlCl₃ is needed in stoichiometric amount in acylation
caveat.statement: In Friedel–Crafts acylation AlCl₃ complexes with the ketone product, so at least one equivalent is used; it is not a true catalyst.

caveat.title: HBr with a peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov
caveat.rule: HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene by Markovnikov's rule.
caveat.statement: In the presence of a peroxide, HBr (and only HBr) adds against Markovnikov’s rule.

caveat.title: Cannizzaro needs an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen
caveat.statement: Aldehydes with an α-hydrogen (such as ethanal) undergo the aldol reaction instead.

caveat.title: Only CH₃–CO– and CH₃–CH(OH)– groups respond
caveat.statement: The iodoform test is positive for methyl ketones, ethanal, ethanol and secondary alcohols of the type CH₃–CH(OH)–R.

caveat.title: PCC stops at the aldehyde
caveat.rule: Primary alcohols are oxidised to carboxylic acids by strong oxidants.
caveat.statement: PCC in anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ stops at the aldehyde stage.
caveat.explanation: Without water no aldehyde hydrate forms, so nothing is oxidised further. Acidified dichromate under reflux goes on to the acid.

caveat.title: Saytzeff product is major with a small base
caveat.rule: Elimination from a haloalkane can give more than one alkene.
caveat.statement: With alcoholic KOH the more substituted alkene (but-2-ene) is the major product.

route.name: Aniline → phenol
route.description: Diazotise at 0–5 °C, then warm the diazonium salt with water.

route.name: Ethanol → propan-2-ol
route.description: Oxidise to ethanal with PCC, then add a methyl Grignard reagent and work up.

relationship.note: Decided by whether the aldehyde has an α-hydrogen.
A different reaction achieving the reverse change.
Same change, different oxidant: PCC is selective, dichromate needs distillation.
Same substrate and base; the solvent tips the balance.
